owner_target: Independent real coordinates with densities <=1; arbitrary real symmetric A with at least three eigenvalues of modulus >=1; prove a universal essential density bound for X^TAX or give a valid counterexample. Continuity separate.

primary_source.theorem_1_2: Independent densities <=K and normalized scalar coefficients imply density <=sqrt(2)K a.e.
primary_source.equation_8_4: For every integer r>=0, S_r(M)^2=sum_{j>r}s_j(M)^2 and L(MY,M0 t S_r(M))<=(C M0 p)^r under coordinate concentration caps.
primary_source.cap_one_conversion: Since L(Y_i,t)<=2t for density cap one under the paper's radius convention, write C_*=2C and obtain P(||MY+alpha||<=u)<=min(1,(C_*u/S_r(M))^r), uniformly in shifts alpha.
primary_source.forbidden_extra_hypotheses: No moments, support, iid, centering, symmetry, log-concavity, smoothness, or post-rotation independence added.

partner_result_actually_used.application: Its inverse-first-moment engine is recovered as the (r,q)=(2,1) instance of the new fractional negative-moment transfer; the new (1,1/2) instance is combined with one genuinely private physical square.

new_results.statement: For cap-one original product Y, integer r>=1 with S_r(M)>0, 0<q<r, and deterministic alpha, sup_alpha E||MY+alpha||^{-q} <= [r/(r-q)](C_*/S_r(M))^q. In particular E||MY+alpha||^{-1/2}<=2 sqrt(C_*/S_1(M)).
For disjoint original banks X,Y and scalar W, T=X^T M Y+alpha^T X+G(Y)+aW^2+h(Y)W+c with a!=0 and S_1(M)>0 has essential density <=2^(9/4)sqrt(C_*)/sqrt(|a|S_1(M)). Generic continuity not claimed.
For original partition I,J,{w},K with A_II=0, A_Iw=0, a=A_ww!=0 and B=A_IJ, every other block arbitrary/retained, ||p_(X^TAX)||inf<=2^(7/4)sqrt(C_*)/sqrt(|a|S_1(B)).

For r_j=n^-1/2(1,sqrt2 cos(2pi j/n),sqrt2 sin(2pi j/n)), A_n=RR^T is a rank-three projection with leverage 3/n, and every nonzero vector in range(R) has support at least n-2. Hence an exact spectral eigen-square cannot be universally extracted on a sparse/private original-coordinate bank.

pinned_result_actually_applied.application: On the harmonic frame A_n=RR^T, G_I=R^TR=I_3 and every normalized leverage is 3/n<=1/2, so ||p_(X^T A_n X)||inf<=12 for every allowed product law. This proves the sparse-private spectral-square failure is a proof-interface obstruction, not a QFORM counterexample. A secondary stress family also uses pinned D5 to get <23.843.

secondary_stress.spectrum: N copies each of +/-(N-1)^(-1/2), plus -1,+1,+1; exactly three eigenvalues have modulus >=1.
secondary_stress.currency: For B=(N-1)^(-1/2)I_N, S_1(B)=1, so the new bound is dimension-free; pinned D5 has Z_5=binom(N,5)/(N-1)^5>=1/1280 and gives <23.843.
